Check: Page title identifies the Login screen
Test Steps: Inspect visible page title and document heading
Expected Result: PASS if exactly one h1 identifies the page as Đăng nhập; otherwise FAIL

Check: All labels and actions use consistent Vietnamese
Test Steps: Read heading, labels, links, and submit action
Expected Result: PASS if uI is consistently Vietnamese except accepted technical terms; otherwise FAIL

Check: Login card is visually aligned and does not overlap
Test Steps: Inspect card, fields, links, and footer
Expected Result: PASS if all elements align with adequate spacing and no overlap; otherwise FAIL

Check: Login remains usable at 320 px width
Test Steps: Inspect and operate the complete form
Expected Result: PASS if no clipping or horizontal page scroll; targets remain usable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Text, links, borders, and button meet WCAG AA contrast
Test Steps: Measure key foreground/background combinations
Expected Result: PASS if normal text ≥4.5:1 and meaningful UI components ≥3:1; otherwise FAIL

Check: Interactive controls have usable pointer targets
Test Steps: Measure fields, links, and submit target areas
Expected Result: PASS if primary controls are at least 44×44 CSS px or equivalently usable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Email control uses native email semantics
Test Steps: Inspect control semantics and enter malformed email
Expected Result: PASS if input type is email and native validation rejects malformed format; otherwise FAIL

Check: Password value is concealed
Test Steps: Type a password and observe its rendering
Expected Result: PASS if control uses password type and characters are masked; otherwise FAIL

Check: Required fields show an asterisk beside the label
Test Steps: Inspect Email and Password labels
Expected Result: PASS if both mandatory labels include a visible required marker; otherwise FAIL

Check: Labels are programmatically associated with inputs
Test Steps: Click labels and inspect accessible names
Expected Result: PASS if each label focuses its input and supplies the accessible name; otherwise FAIL

Check: Empty required fields show visible form validation
Requirement or Heuristic Source: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1, 3.3.3; WAI Forms; GOV.UK Error message — https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/ | https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/
Test Steps: Submit without entering values and inspect the visible form response
Expected Result: PASS if visible validation identifies both required fields near their controls; otherwise FAIL

Check: Tab order follows top-to-bottom reading order
Test Steps: Press Tab from browser chrome through all controls
Expected Result: PASS if focus order is Email, Password, Forgot password, Submit, Register; otherwise FAIL

Check: Every interactive element has visible keyboard focus
Test Steps: Tab through every control
Expected Result: PASS if a persistent, high-contrast focus indicator is visible; otherwise FAIL

Check: Controls expose correct autocomplete semantics
Preconditions: Login page open with password manager available
Test Steps: Inspect autocomplete and try saved-credential fill
Expected Result: PASS if email and current password can be filled into the correct fields; otherwise FAIL

Check: Form remains usable at 200% browser zoom
Test Steps: Set zoom to 200% and operate form
Expected Result: PASS if no content or focus indicator is clipped; reflow remains usable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Layout remains coherent under right-to-left direction
Test Steps: Inspect order, alignment, clipping, and focus sequence
Expected Result: PASS if no text, control, or focus indicator overlaps or becomes unreachable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Repeated submit shows a clear pending state
Requirement or Heuristic Source: Nielsen H1; WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3; ARIA APG Alert — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/
Test Steps: Submit once, then immediately double-click the button and press Enter repeatedly
Expected Result: PASS if the submit control visibly indicates a pending state and prevents repeated activation; otherwise FAIL

Check: Each visible order row includes ID, date, total, and current status
Preconditions: Account has at least one order
Test Steps: Inspect every displayed order row
Expected Result: PASS if every row visibly contains all four FR-11 fields; otherwise FAIL

Check: Newest order is easy to identify
Test Steps: Compare displayed order sequence with dates/IDs
Expected Result: PASS if orders are sorted newest first or sorting is clearly provided; otherwise FAIL

Check: Totals use deterministic Vietnamese VND format
Preconditions: Account has orders with varied totals
Test Steps: Inspect totals across rows and browser locales
Expected Result: PASS if values use Vietnamese thousands separators and ₫ consistently; otherwise FAIL

Check: Dates use an unambiguous Vietnamese format
Test Steps: Inspect dates across browsers/locales
Expected Result: PASS if day, month, and year are unambiguous and consistent; otherwise FAIL

Check: All five order states have clear Vietnamese labels
Preconditions: Test data covers pending confirmed shipping delivered canceled
Test Steps: Inspect label for each state
Expected Result: PASS if every backend state maps to the specified Vietnamese meaning; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order states are visually distinguishable
Test Steps: Compare status badges
Expected Result: PASS if states are consistently distinguishable and remain readable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Cancel requires explicit confirmation
Test Steps: Activate Hủy đơn
Expected Result: PASS if a confirmation dialog names the consequence before mutation; otherwise FAIL

Check: Cancel action is fully keyboard operable
Test Steps: Focus and activate cancel; operate confirmation
Expected Result: PASS if action and dialog work without pointer and focus returns logically; otherwise FAIL

Check: Signed-in user can independently find order history
Test Steps: Navigate using visible UI without direct URL
Expected Result: PASS if profile/order history entry is clearly discoverable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Navigation indicates the current Profile/History location
Test Steps: Inspect navbar state
Expected Result: PASS if current destination is visually and programmatically indicated; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order retrieval shows a clear loading state
Requirement or Heuristic Source: Nielsen H1; WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3; ARIA APG Alert — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/
Test Steps: Open /profile
Expected Result: PASS if a non-blocking loading indicator appears until data resolves; otherwise FAIL

Check: Status meaning does not depend on color alone
Test Steps: Inspect in grayscale and with screen reader
Expected Result: PASS if readable text communicates every state independently of color; otherwise FAIL

Check: Table headers are associated with their data cells
Requirement or Heuristic Source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1; ARIA APG Table; GOV.UK Table — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/ | https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/table/
Test Steps: Inspect accessibility tree and navigate by screen reader
Expected Result: PASS if table has caption/context, column headers, and correct associations; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order history remains usable at 320 px width
Test Steps: Read all fields and access eligible actions
Expected Result: PASS if table reflows or provides controlled scroll without page-wide clipping; otherwise FAIL

Check: History remains readable at 200% zoom/text scaling
Test Steps: Set zoom/text to 200% and inspect/operate
Expected Result: PASS if labels, totals, status, and actions remain visible and usable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order API failure is distinct from a genuine empty history
Test Steps: Open /profile and retry if offered
Expected Result: PASS if clear error and recovery action appear; empty-state message is not shown; otherwise FAIL

Check: Cancel action shows timely visible success or failure feedback
Requirement or Heuristic Source: Nielsen H1; WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3; ARIA APG Alert — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/
Test Steps: Perform a cancel action once under success conditions and once under failure conditions
Expected Result: PASS if visible feedback clearly communicates success or failure without ambiguity; otherwise FAIL

Check: Each visible validation error is associated with its input
Test Steps: Submit each field with invalid or missing input; inspect the accessibility tree and move focus to the field
Expected Result: PASS if each error is visible, names the affected field, and is programmatically associated with that field; otherwise FAIL

Check: A dynamically displayed login error is announced without moving focus unexpectedly
Preconditions: Screen reader running; credentials produce a visible error
Test Steps: Submit once and listen to the screen reader while observing keyboard focus
Expected Result: PASS if the complete error is announced and focus remains at a logical control; otherwise FAIL

Check: Focused login controls are not hidden by other content
Preconditions: Login page open at desktop and 320 px viewport
Test Steps: Tab through every interactive control at both viewports
Expected Result: PASS if every focused control and its focus indicator remain at least partially visible; otherwise FAIL

Check: Login content remains readable with WCAG text-spacing overrides
Test Steps: Apply line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em, and word spacing 0.16em
Expected Result: PASS if no label, link, input value, error, or button text is clipped or overlaps; otherwise FAIL

Check: Login is usable in portrait and landscape orientation
Test Steps: Open the page in portrait, rotate to landscape, and complete all form interactions
Expected Result: PASS if the same controls and content remain available and usable in both orientations; otherwise FAIL

Check: Login remains readable when browser or OS dark mode is forced
Preconditions: Browser or OS forced dark mode available
Test Steps: Enable forced dark mode; inspect normal, focused, and error states
Expected Result: PASS if all text, controls, focus indicators, and errors remain visible and distinguishable; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order table has a programmatically associated descriptive caption
Preconditions: Order History contains at least one order
Test Steps: Inspect the table accessibility tree and navigate to the table with a screen reader
Expected Result: PASS if the table exposes a concise accessible caption identifying it as order history; otherwise FAIL

Check: Order information has a logical reading order at desktop and mobile widths
Test Steps: Read the table with a screen reader at desktop width, then at 320 px width
Expected Result: PASS if each row is announced in the visible column order without detached or repeated values; otherwise FAIL

Check: Cancel confirmation keeps keyboard focus within the modal until it closes
Preconditions: A visible cancel control opens a modal confirmation
Test Steps: Open the dialog by keyboard; press Tab and Shift+Tab through controls; close with each available method
Expected Result: PASS if focus enters the dialog, cycles within it, and returns to the invoking control after close; otherwise FAIL

Check: A wide order table does not cause page-wide horizontal scrolling
Preconditions: Order History populated; viewport 320 CSS px
Test Steps: Scroll vertically and horizontally through the page and table region
Expected Result: PASS if any required horizontal scrolling is confined to the table region and surrounding page content reflows; otherwise FAIL

Check: A visible order-state change is announced to assistive technology
Preconditions: An action causes a visible order-state update
Test Steps: Trigger the action once while a screen reader is running
Expected Result: PASS if the updated state or confirmation is announced without requiring focus movement; otherwise FAIL
